## Hand scan of 146

οἳ δ’ ἀμφὶ Πρίαμον καὶ Πάνθοον ἠδὲ Θυμοίτην. Fifteen syllables: οἳ δ’ἀμ (– –) | φὶ Πρί α (– ⏑ ⏑, φὶ long by position before Πρ, as regularly before Πρίαμος) | μον καὶ (– –) | Πάν θο ον (– ⏑ ⏑) | ἠ δὲ Θυ (– ⏑ ⏑) | μοί την (– ×). The scanner reports the same pattern and no other fit exists. The scanner's "long scanned short" and UNRESOLVED come from Θυ-: the υ of θυμός is long, and the line needs it short. Whether the name belongs with θυμός is not known, so the line is irregular only if it does; the sentence is added as the runbook asks, on the precedent of iliad-015 Μυρίνης (814).

## Flagged judgement calls

- **118–119 ἄρν’ singular: kept.** The dual of 103 (ἄρν’ with ἕτερον … ἑτέρην) is fixed by the two adjectives that follow it. At 119 the object of ἐκέλευεν οἰσέμεναι stands alone, the first pair is already being fetched by Hector’s heralds (ἄρνάς, 117), and 104 leaves one victim (ἄλλον) for the Achaeans to bring. "A lamb" is the best-supported reading; `l`, `i` and the row in `new-renderings.md` stand; the note now shows the alternative.
- **162–163 ἴδῃ: kept.** Priam is addressing Helen, so the subject is "you"; ἴδῃ is the contracted second-person middle subjunctive (the same verb as ἴδηαι at 130, and the note says so). A third-person active reading ("that he/she may see") has no subject in the sentence. `l` and `i` "you may see" stand.
- **162 ἐμεῖο: kept.** The note gives both readings (with ἵζευ "by me", or with πάροιθ’ "in front of me"); `l` and `i` "sit down by me" suit either, and "sit before me" is turned down in `new-renderings.md` because it would decide the question. No change except the participle in `l` (above).

## Findings considered and refused

- **84–85 ἐσσυμένως "goes with both verbs" (note, 84).** Grammatically it can only stand with one clause, but the claim is soft and the English "hurriedly" / "in haste" is what the line gives; no change.
- **103 ἄρν’ "two lambs" from the dual, and "male and female".** Rests on ἕτερον (neuter/masculine) and ἑτέρην (feminine) and on the dual; the note shows the grounds. Kept.
- **163 πρότερον "former" vs an adverb "first".** The same word is "former" at 140 (ἀνδρός … προτέρου, where it is certainly an adjective); here the adjective agrees with πόσιν. The adverb reading is possible but not better; kept, as in the table row.
- **166 ὥς "so that".** The accent is the proclitic ὡς before the enclitic μοι, not a demonstrative; "so that … you may name" stands.
- **168 `i` drops καί of καὶ μείζονες ("even taller").** In `i` "Others are indeed taller by a head" keeps the sense; καί is kept in `l` and the note. Refused as idiom.
- **109 `i` "where an old man is among them" for οἷς … ὁ γέρων.** `l` keeps "among whom … the old man"; `i` reads naturally and keeps the general sense. Refused.
- **113 `i` "got out themselves" supplies the chariots.** It does not name them (the note says the Greek does not); "got out" is the plain sense of ἐκ … ἔβαν. Refused.
- **138 `i` turns the dative "to him who has won" into "of the one who wins".** The sense is the same in English; `l` keeps the dative. Refused.
- **92–93 against iliad-016.** `l` and `i` are verbatim those of the published unit; the missing comma after γένηται means the whole-unit rule does not apply, as `new-renderings.md` says. Nothing to change.
- **Epithets and formulas.** κρείων, δῖος "heavenly", ἐϋκνήμιδες "well-greaved", ἀρηΐφιλος, βοὴν ἀγαθός, λευκώλενος, βοῶπις, ὄζος Ἄρηος, ἠΰς τε μέγας τε (iliad-013, 2.653) and the 129 and 143 repeats all agree with the table and the published units.
